Microsoft Copilot

AI assistant embedded across Microsoft 365 - Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams and Windows - grounded in your organisation's own tenant data via Microsoft Graph.

Visit official website ↗Explore pricing & limits

OverviewFeaturesUse casesPricingTradeoffsCompatibilityFAQ

What is Microsoft Copilot?

AI assistant embedded across Microsoft 365 - Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams and Windows - grounded in your organisation's own tenant data via Microsoft Graph. Also available as a free consumer chat assistant.

Best for

Organisations whose day already runs through Outlook, Teams, Word and Excel.

Main features

  • Copilot in Word (draft/rewrite/summarise), Excel (formulas, analysis, charts), PowerPoint (deck generation), Outlook (triage and drafting), Teams (meeting recap and action items)
  • Copilot Chat (web-grounded, no extra cost)
  • Copilot Studio for custom agents
  • Agent 365
  • Copilot Credits for metered agent work.

Practical use cases

  • Meeting recaps and action items from Teams
  • inbox triage in Outlook
  • first-draft documents grounded in SharePoint content
  • Excel analysis
  • deck generation from a Word doc
  • custom agents over internal data.

Who is it for?

  • Organisations already standardised on Microsoft 365; enterprise IT, finance, HR, sales and operations teams.

Pricing, free access & limits

Per-user add-on licence on top of a qualifying Microsoft 365 base plan; plus consumption-based Copilot Credits

Plans described in the source

Microsoft 365 Copilot (Enterprise) $30/user/mo, annual commitment - requires a qualifying base licence (E3, E5, Business Standard/Premium, E1, F1/F3). Microsoft 365 Copilot Business $21/user/mo annual ($25.20 monthly) for orgs up to 300 users; a promotional $18/user/mo runs 1 July - 31 December 2026 (annual commitment, first year only, not on trials). Bundles introduced 1 July 2026: Business Standard + Copilot $23.50/user/mo; Business Premium + Copilot $32/user/mo; E7 Frontier Suite $99/user/mo. Copilot Studio from $200/mo per tenant. Copilot Credits $0.01 each pay-as-you-go, or $200 for 25,000 credits/mo prepaid.

Free plan

Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is included at no extra per-user cost for many M365 users (web-grounded chat only, not in-app Copilot). A free consumer Copilot app also exists.

Free trial

Trials available through Microsoft and partners; promotional pricing explicitly excluded from trial subscriptions.

Usage limits to consider

Copilot cannot be bought standalone - a qualifying M365 licence is mandatory. Business SKU capped at 300 users and Microsoft can enforce that limit. Agent actions consume Copilot Credits, so complex multi-step tasks cost more than simple ones. Pay-as-you-go credits require an Azure subscription.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Tenant-grounded answers using your real documents and email
  • unmatched depth inside Office apps
  • enterprise-grade compliance, data residency and admin controls
  • no data leaves the Microsoft compliance boundary.

Limitations to consider

  • The $30 headline is never the total - add the base suite and the real all-in figure is roughly $66-90/user/mo on E3/E5. Every assigned seat costs the same whether used or not
  • Microsoft reports ~15M paid seats against 450M+ commercial users (~3.3% penetration). Gartner's 2026 assessment says value realisation is not guaranteed.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Windows, web, iOS, Android, Microsoft 365 desktop and web apps, Teams, Edge

Languages

  • Broad Microsoft 365 language coverage incl. Arabic, French, English

API access

Indirect - Copilot Studio, Microsoft Graph API, Azure AI Foundry

Integrations and exports

  • Entire Microsoft 365 / Graph estate, SharePoint, OneDrive, Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Teams
  • third-party connectors via Copilot Studio

Evaluation notes

In most small offices only two to four people per ten get real value - typically those whose day is the inbox, the Teams meeting and long Word/Excel files. Licensing the rest is how a $756 decision becomes a $2,520 one.
